answer: Each agent must lock a slashable bond before its vote or payout counts. A public ledger ties that bond to one identity and a random audit schedule; if an account is caught faking its identity, the deposit is burned. Reaching the zenith of influence therefore costs an attacker one full bond per forged agent, plus the constant risk of losing every bond at once when auditors check. Even a velvet facade of polite newcomers leaves a marble trail of funded deposits, so buying a thousand identities means paying a thousand bonds up front.
